newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE Nov coffee futures dive on supply concerns.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE Nov coffee futures dive on supply concerns.

text.p: London's robusta coffee contract retraced to end sharply lower on Tuesday with the spot November contract taking the brunt of the losses.
Spot November was down by a hefty 7.12 percent, or $121, on the day to end at $1,460 a tonne.
Traders said perceptions of growing prompt supplies led long holders to liquidate some of their November positions ahead of the Friday expiry.
"Everybody is talking of more coffee coming in," a trader said. "It has started showing up in the tenders and the amount of coffee which is graded."
Benchmark January stood $16 lower at $1,406 on scale-up
trade and origin selling, but traders noted some scale-down roaster buying support at around $1,420.
The closely-watched Nov/Jan spread shrank significantly to $38 at one stage, before closing at $54 and compared with Monday's finish of $148.
LIFFE said some 1,237 lots have been graded in November of which 426 were untenderable. Tenders stood at 834, of which eight were retenders.

Exchange volume was 4,549 lots, centred on January and March contracts. Latest crop forecasts by German statistician F.O. Licht released earlier on Tuesday was at the lower end of market expectations, traders said.
In its first estimate of world coffee crop, Licht put total output at 96.45 million 60-kg bags in the 1996/97 crop year against 87.64 million in 1995/96.

Licht put the Brazilian crop at 26 million bags, up by more than 10 million but well below some estimates, traders said. "For example, there were 6.24 million bags of Brazilian arrivals in the first four months of the 1996/97 crop from July to October, which is nearly three times the arrivals in the same period last year," said a trader at a major trade house.
"It is also seven percent above arrivals in 1994/95, which turned out to be a crop of 28 million bags," the trader said.
Traders said rainfall distribution was above average across many coffee areas and this also meant a good crop for 1997/98.
